rubric.why: Identifies that a dynamic equilibrium involves reactions continuing in both directions.
rubric.description: At dynamic equilibrium, the reaction continues in both directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the reaction continues in both directions.

rubric.why: States the constant concentrations at dynamic equilibrium or contrasts this with no change at static equilibrium.
rubric.description: The concentrations of reacting species remain constant; in static equilibrium, no change takes place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the constant concentrations or the absence of change in static equilibrium.

modelAnswer: At dynamic equilibrium, the reaction keeps on going in both the directions, and the concentrations of reacting species remain constant. In static equilibrium, no change is taking place.

rubric.why: Identifies product removal as the action that shifts a reversible reaction toward completion.
rubric.description: Withdraw one or all products from the reaction mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one or all products are withdrawn or removed.

rubric.why: States that prompt product removal drives the reaction in the forward direction.
rubric.description: Remove the products as soon as they are formed, driving the reaction forward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the timing of removal or for stating that the reaction is driven forward.

modelAnswer: Withdraw one or all the products from the reaction mixture as soon as they are formed. The reaction is then driven in the forward direction.

rubric.why: Identifies a catalyst and its effect on both reaction directions.
rubric.description: A catalyst increases the rates of both forward and backward reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a catalyst increases both rates.

rubric.why: Connects the increased reaction rates to reaching equilibrium in less time.
rubric.description: A catalyst decreases the time taken to attain equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a catalyst reduces the time to reach equilibrium.

modelAnswer: A catalyst increases both the rates of forward and backward reactions of a reversible reaction. So if a reversible reaction is carried out in the presence of a catalyst it will decrease the time taken by the reaction to attain the state of equilibrium.

rubric.why: Identifies that the combustion products do not react with one another.
rubric.description: The products formed do not react among themselves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the products do not react among themselves.

rubric.why: States that the products cannot regenerate the reactants under the original conditions.
rubric.description: The products do not give back the reactants under the same conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the reactants are not re-formed under the same conditions.

modelAnswer: Combustion reactions are generally irreversible because the products formed do not react among themselves to give back the reactants under the same conditions.

rubric.why: Describes how the forward reaction begins and product build-up gives rise to the reverse reaction.
rubric.description: The forward reaction starts first; as products build up, they react to give back reactants in the reverse reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that products build up and react in the reverse direction, or that the forward reaction starts first.

rubric.why: States the condition reached as equilibrium is approached.
rubric.description: Both reactions continue until their rates become equal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the forward and backward rates become equal.

modelAnswer: The forward reaction starts first. As products build up, they react to give back the reactants in the reverse reaction. Both reactions continue until the rate of forward reaction becomes equal to the rate of backward reaction.

rubric.why: Identifies withdrawal of products as the means of forcing the reversible reaction onward.
rubric.description: Withdraw one or all products from the reaction mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one or all products are withdrawn or removed.

rubric.why: States that products must be removed as they form to force the reaction to completion.
rubric.description: Withdraw the products as soon as they are formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that products are removed as soon as they form.

modelAnswer: A reversible reaction may be forced to go to completion if one or all the products are withdrawn from the reaction mixture as soon as they are formed.
